<entry id="M00426">
<head-word>מוֹהֶה</head-word>
<head-word>מוֹהִי</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, a disguise of מֹשֶׁה.</definition>
<notes> Ned. I, 2 (10
<sup>a</sup>) נדר במ' (Mish. ed. במותא, Bab. ed. נודר בסוהי; corr. acc.) if one says, A vow by (that of) Mohi; Tosef. ib. I, 2 האומר מוחה ודאי מוחו ed. Zuck. (Var. מוהי … מוהה, מוהו, a. ודאמר for ודאי) read: האומר מ' ודאמר מ' if one says, (
<italic>Neder</italic>) 
<italic>Mohi</italic>, or (
<italic>Neder</italic>) 
<italic>d’ămar Mohi</italic>, the vow of M. or the vow which M. uttered; expl. Y. ib. I, 37
<sup>a</sup> top [read:] בנדר דנדר מ' במומי דנדר משה וכ' by the vow which M. vowed, that means, by the oath which Moses vowed, as we read (Ex. II, 2</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> &c.; Bab. ib. 10
<sup>b</sup> האומר במ' לא אמר כלום if a person said, by Mohi, he said nothing, but if he says, by the oath which M.</definition>
<notes> spoke &c. Ib. 22
<sup>b</sup> אי נדרת במ' וכ' if thou hadst vowed by M. (using the phrase נדר מ') &c.—[מוֹהִי 
<italic>water</italic>, v. מוֹי.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="M00431">
<head-word>מוֹהַר</head-word>
<head-word>מֹהַר</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> מָהַר)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>exchange</italic>, esp. 
<italic>the price paid for the wife;</italic> (in later practice) 
<italic>the wife’s settlement, widowhood</italic> (כתובה).</definition>
<notes> Mekh. Mishp., N’zikin, s. 17 (ref. to Ex. XXII, 15) מלמד שהוא עוֹשָׂהּ עליו מ' this indicates that he (the father) imposes it upon him (the seducer) as a 
<italic>mohar</italic>; ואין מ' אלא כתובה וכ' and 
<italic>mohar</italic> means 
<italic>k’thubah</italic>, as we read (Gen. XXXIV, 12) &c.; Y. Keth. III, 27
<sup>d</sup> top (read אותה for אותן). Bab. ib. 10
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Ex. XXII, 16) שיהא זה כמ' הבתולות וכ' that this (fine) be equal to the indemnity for outraged virginity (Deut. XXII, 29), and the settlement of virgins be like this (indemnity, i.e. fifty Shekel silver); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. מוֹהֲרִין,</plural-form> constr. מוֹהֲרֵי. Y. ib. III, beg. 27
<sup>a</sup> [read:] אילו היה כתיב כמוֹהֲרֵי בתולות יאות if it read, like the indemnities for virgins, it might be right (as you say).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup> בריאה במ' ואבורגני (Rabad פרהגבני, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 60) a lease is sound if made legal by sureties and (countersigned) by officers. Oth. explan., v. אַבּוּרְגְּנָא.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="M00458">
<head-word>מוּט</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to incline, waver, decline; to give way, bend</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Snh. X, 27
<sup>d</sup> bot., v. infra. Tanḥ. B’har 1 כשתָּמוּט ידם לפני וכ' when their power shall sink before Nebuchadnezzar. Tanḥ. Vayishl. 3 (ref. to Prov. XXV, 26) כשמָט לפני וכ' when he bends (humiliates himself) before the wicked; Gen. R. s. 75 א"א לצדיק לָמוּט וכ' (Yalk. Gen. 130 לִימּוֹט) it is impossible to the righteous to bend &c.; a. e.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִמּוֹט</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be shaken, bent</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yalk. l. c., v. supra.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הֵמִיט</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to bend, to shake.</italic></definition>
<notes> Zab. III, 3 כל שאינה יכולה להָמִיט באדם (not בה אדם) (Asheri להָסִיט, v. סוּט) a ship which has no staggering effect on man. Gen. R. l. c. מֵמִיט עצמו וכ' humbles himself.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpol.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְמוֹטֵט, </binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, 
<italic>Nithpol</italic>.</definition>
<notes> נִתְמוֹטֵט 
<italic>to be declining; to sink</italic>. Y. Snh. X, 27
<sup>d</sup> bot.; Yalk. Is. 338 (ref. to Is. LIV, 10) אם ראית זכות אבות שמָטָה … שנִתְמוֹטְטָה וכ' when thou seest the merit of the fathers decline and that of the mothers sink, go and cling to grace; Lev. R. s. 36, end שנִתְמֹטְטָה.—Y. l. c. 28
<sup>b</sup> והיו מִתְמוֹטְטִין והולכין they sank deeper and deeper (into poverty). B. Mets. 71
<sup>a</sup> נכסיו מתמוטטין (Ms. M. מתמעטין) his wealth will be reduced; Yalk. Ps. 665 מִתְמוֹטֵט he will sink. B. Mets. l. c. הללו מתמ' וכ' (Ms. R. 2 מוֹטְטִין, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. notes 2—4) these sink and rise again &c.; Yalk. l. c.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="M00515">

<xref rid="M00340">מָה</xref>,
<language-reference>

<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>something, anything</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ned. 66
<sup>b</sup>, v. יָפֶה.—Y. Kidd. III, 64
<sup>c</sup> bot. מהו ממזר מום זר what is 
<italic>mamzer</italic> (מַמְזֵר)? Something repulsive; Yeb. 76
<sup>b</sup> ממזר כתיב מ' זר the Law says 
<italic>mamzer</italic> which means anything repulsive (male or female); Sifré Deut. 248 כל שהוא מומזר (corr. acc.) whatever is in any way repulsive.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>blemish</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Bekh. V, 5, a. fr. בעל מ' having a blemish (unfit for the altar, for priestly service &c.). Ib. VI, 9, a. fr. הרי זה מ' this is a legal blemish; אינה מ' this is not &c.—Meg. 29
<sup>a</sup>, v. יָהִיר. B. Mets. 59
<sup>b</sup> מ' שבך וכ' do not reproach thy neighbor with a fault which is also thine own; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. מוּמִין</plural-form>. Bekh. VI, 1 על אלו מ' וכ' these are the blemishes in consequence of which a first-born animal may be slaughtered (after the destruction of the Temple). Ib. 2 אין מ' בלבן a blemish in the white of the eye is no blemish in the sense of the law. Ib. VII, 1 מ' אלו … פוסלין וכ' the above named blemishes, whether permanent or transitory, make also human beings unfit (for priesthood &c.); a. fr.—Denom. הוּמָם 
<italic>to become blemished, defective</italic>. Y. Shek. IV, 48
<sup>b</sup> שפודין תמימין והוּמְמוּ they had redeemed them when they were without blemish, and they became blemished. Num. R. s. 12, end; Cant. R. to VI, 4 ולא הוממו וכ' and they have not become unfit for sacrifices on account of blemishes or old age &c., v. זָהַם.—Y. Yoma II, 39
<sup>d</sup> קטורת שכבת הוּמָמָה frankincense which was extinguished is unfit for the altar.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>b</sup> קמיע שאינו מ' an unapproved amulet; Tosef. ib. IV (V), 10 מוּמְחָא. Sabb. l. c. מ' לאדם of approved effect on human beings. Y. ib. VI, 8
<sup>b</sup> top קמיע זה מ' this amulet is approved.—Erub. V, 5 (58
<sup>b</sup>) אלא מן המ' (Ms. O. אלא מ', v. Rashi a. l.) only one of the best of the expert class; (oth. opin. v. Bart. a. l.).—Gen. R. s. 30 צדיק ומ' a righteous man and at the same time a practical man; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. מוּמְחִים, מוּמְחִין</plural-form>. Snh. III, 1 (23
<sup>a</sup>) כשרים (או) מ' (Bab. a. Y. ed. מ' מפי ב"ד, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />
<notes> men otherwise qualified and (or) authorized by the court; expl. ib. 23
<sup>a</sup> אם היו כשרין נעשו כמ' if not disqualified (on account of kinship or bad conduct) they are to be considered as if they were authorized judges; a. e.—[מומחה, מומחא, Sabb. 58

<definition> (עוּד)

<italic>an animal whose owner stands forewarned</italic> on account of three successive injuries;

<notes> B. Kam. I, 4 שור המ' an ox that has done damage three times. Ib. השן מ' לאכול וכ' the tooth of an animal is considered a 
<italic>muʿad</italic> with reference to eating such things as are fit to be eaten by it, i.e. damages for eating must be paid in full without previous forewarning. Ib. הרגל מ' לשבר וכ' the foot is a 
<italic>muʿad</italic> &c., i.e. what an animal treads upon on its way must be paid for in full without forewarning. Ib. הנחש מ' לעולם the serpent is always a 
<italic>muʿad</italic> (even when tamed). Ib. מ' משלם נזק שלם וכ' the 
<italic>muʿad</italic> pays full damage, collectible from the owner’s best property. Ib. II, 4 מ' כל שהעידו וכ' a 
<italic>muʿad</italic> is an animal against which three warnings on three days have been given; (another opin.) מ' שהעידו … פעמים against which three warnings have been given (even in one day). Ib. 5 אדם מ' לעולם damage done by a human being must under all circumstances be restored in full. Ib. 17
<sup>b</sup> (הידוס) הרי זה מ' damage done by chickens must be restored in full; אינו מ' must not &c.; a. v. fr.—Trnsf. מ' לעבירה a 
<italic>muʿad</italic> for sin, i.e. 
<italic>likely to sin again</italic>. Num. R. s. 9 כיון שנשתלש בחטא נעשה מ' לע' having sinned three times, he has become a

<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (= מְמ'; מָעַט) 
<italic>small, minute, sparse</italic>.</definition>
<notes> דבר מ' 
<italic>a little</italic>; 
<italic>small</italic> (
<italic>spot</italic> &c.). Tosef. Sot. XV, 12, sq.; Tosef. B. Bath. II, 17 משייר בה ד' מ' leaves a little portion (of the wall) unfinished in remembrance of the destruction of Jerusalem; משיירת ד' מ' leaves off a little portion of her toilet. Ḥag. I, 5 זה וזה מ' if he has little of both. Ib. 8 שהן מקרא מ' the Biblical text for these laws is sparse. Gitt. 14
<sup>a</sup> מתנה מ' a small gift. Sifra Tsav, ch. XV, Par. 11 סמיכה מ' the putting on of hands which is rarer (than waving, being confined only to live sacrifices); תנופה מ' waving which is rarer (being performed by one person only, while putting hands on is done by all sharers in the sacrifice); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. מוּעָטִים, מוּעָטִין; מוּעָטוֹת</plural-form>. Ḥag. l. c. אוכלים מרובים ונכסים מ' many eaters (members of the household partaking of the peace-offering) and small wealth. Ib. עולות מ' less burnt-offerings (than peace-offerings). Ib. 11
<sup>a</sup> מקרא … והלכות מ' the Rabbinical laws sparse in comparison to the profuse Bible text on the subject. Arakh. 30
<sup>b</sup> וכי יש … שנים מ' are there longer and shorter years?; a. fr.—Esp. מוּעָט, מְמוּעָט 
<italic>the smaller thing, the lesser sphere</italic>. R. Hash. 4
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. תפסת מרובה לא תפסת תפסת מ' תפסת if you take hold of the larger thing, you may lose your hold, if of the smaller, you will hold it, i.e. where the interpretation is doubtful, select the smaller number; Y. Yoma II, end, 40
<sup>a</sup> הממ'. Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., ch. XIII, Par. XII הממ' the least portion thereof. Y. Keth. III, 27
<sup>d</sup> bot. בושת הקטן ממ' the disgrace of a minor is the less grave thing; ib. ונזקי ממ' and the indemnity he gets, is smaller; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>a child whose power of discrimination is uncertain</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tem. 2
<sup>b</sup> לרבות מ' הסמוך לאיש 
<italic>ish</italic> (Lev. l. c.) is used in connection with vows (ערכיו) in order to include ‘a doubtful person next to a man’, i.e. a boy near the age of religious majority; Num. R. s. 10; Naz. 62
<sup>a</sup>; a. e.—Ib. 29
<sup>b</sup> מ' סמוך לאיש דרבנן the rule that the vow of a boy of twelve years of age is valid is merely a rabbinical enactment.—2) 
<italic>distinguished</italic>, esp. 
<italic>mufla</italic>, a special expert assessor at court to whom questions of law are referred, 
<italic>instructing judge</italic>. Hor. I, 4 (if a court gave a wrong decision) לא היה מ' של ב"ד שם in the absence of the 
<italic>mufla</italic>. Ib. 4

<italic>mufla</italic> was absent, they cannot be made responsible for their decision, because they ought to have informed themselves and did not do so (therefore their judgment was not a legal act at all). Y. Snh. I, 19

<italic>mufla</italic> of the court (to whom the question had been referred) went to &c.; Tosef. ib VII, 1; Tosef. Ḥag. II, 9 מופלג ed. Zuck. (Var. מופלא). Sifré Deut. 152 (ref. to יפלא, Deut. XVII, 8) מלמד שבמ' הכתוב מדבר this intimates that the text speaks of the 
<italic>mufla;</italic> Snh. 87
<sup>a</sup> top (Rashi: = מומחה). Cant. R. to III, 7; Num. R. s. 11 (ref. to סריס, II Kings XXV, 19) זה מ' של ב"ד וכ' the 
<italic>saris</italic> means the 
<italic>mufla</italic> of the court, who is called 
<italic>saris</italic> (mediator) &c., v. סָרַס II.—
<plural-form>Pl. מוּפְלָאִין</plural-form>. Hor. 7
<sup>a</sup> Ms. M. a. Rashi (ed. מוּפְלִין). Midr. Till. to Ps. l. c. מוּפְלָאֵי ב"ד.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

(misunderstood by Abbaye as meaning, ‘where is it intimated that an animal must be kept in an enclosed space for some time before it can be offered on the altar?’—and corrected as meaning, ‘where is it intimated that an animal designated for idolatry is forbidden for the Jewish altar?’).—Tosef. Ab. Zar. V (VI), 10 איזה מ' מ' לע"ז וכ' what is meant by 
<italic>m</italic>. (as forbidden for the altar)? That which has been set aside (in a special place designated for the purpose) for idolatrous use, but if one merely devoted it by word of mouth &c. Tem. VI, 1. Tosef. l. c. 9 מאימתי נקרא מ' משנעשה וכ' when is an animal called 
<italic>m</italic>. (for idolatry)? From the time that an act (of dedication) has 
<pgbrk id="pg748" />been done with it; Tem. 29
<sup>a</sup> (בו) אין מ' אסור אלא עד שיעבדו (v. Rashi’s first interpret.; second interpret.:) a 
<italic>m</italic>. remains forbidden only until it has been used for some work (whereby its designation for the idolatrous altar is annulled). Ib. אין מ' אסור … מעשה a 
<italic>m</italic>. remains forbidden only until some act (as shearing its wool or some work) has been done with it; a. e.—4) (Sabbath law) 
<italic>muktseh, that which is not counted on for use on the Sabbath or Holy Day</italic> (v. מוּכָן s. v. כּוּן, a. הַזְמָנָה); 
<italic>forbidden for use</italic> or 
<italic>handling</italic>. Bets. 2
<sup>a</sup> מאי טעמייהו דב"ש מ' הוא what reason had Beth Shammai (to permit the egg laid on the Holy Day by a hen which is kept for laying eggs and can, therefore, not be used for consumption on that day)? Is it not 
<italic>muktseh?</italic> Ib. דאית ליה מ' אית ליה נולד he who forbids 
<italic>m</italic>. forbids also 
<italic>nolad</italic> (v. יָלַד). Sabb. 44
<sup>a</sup> מ' מחמת מיאוס not counted on (and therefore forbidden to handle) on account of its repulsiveness (e. g. an old clay candlestick); מ' מחמת איסור 
<italic>m</italic>. in consequence of a ritual prohibition (e. g. a candlestick which on the entrance of the Sabbath could not be moved because a light was burning on it). Ib. 157
<sup>a</sup> מ' מחמת חסרון כיס not counted on for use on the Sabbath because the object is too expensive for a use for which it is not originally made; a. fr.—
<italic>Pl.</italic> מוּקְצִים, מוּקְצִין 
<italic>set apart, chosen</italic>. Sifré Num. 85 (ref. to בקצה, Num. XI, 1) במ' שבהם the fire seized the distinguished among them (with ref. to קצין, Jud. XI, 11; Yalk. Num. 732 בקצינים).—
<italic>Fem</italic>. מוּקְצָה, 
<plural-form>pl. מוּקְצוֹת</plural-form>. Sabb. 43
<sup>b</sup> והא מ' נינהו are they not
